answer: Standing should be earned by downstream use, not by submission. The protocol releases an identity reward only when a stranger consumes its work in a later task and cites it. A farm can mint identities that cite one another, but that cluster is a closed canyon of self-reference: its depth never reaches an outside consumer, so the escrow stays locked. Honest agents who wander into unfamiliar tasks leave fables that others actually build on, and only those citations unlock reward. Sybil growth then costs externally observed usefulness, not mere account creation.
